summary: Jin som mok (จิ้นส้มหมก) is northern Thai fermented pork cooked in a banana-leaf parcel, often mixed with egg and steamed or grilled. Try it as a shared side when a Chiang Mai restaurant has it; Han Thueng Chiang Mai is a convenient, well-established northern-food option near Wat Umong, though current menu availability is not confirmed.
whyGo: A tangy, savory taste of northern Thai home cooking, with the leaf parcel adding aroma and the cooking softening the fermented pork.
Han Thueng serves a broad selection of regional small plates, so the dish can fit into a sampling meal with sticky rice and other northern specialties.
bestFor: Curious omnivores and groups sharing several dishes.
Visitors exploring the Wat Umong/Suthep area who want a sit-down northern Thai meal.
skipIf: You avoid pork, fermented foods, or possible egg; confirm ingredients and preparation with staff.
You need a guaranteed dish-specific allergen or vegetarian menu.
duration: Allow 60–90 minutes for a meal and travel within the Suthep/Wat Umong area; this is a planning estimate.
cost: The exact jin som mok price is not published in the sources checked. Recent restaurant listing data places a meal around ฿251–500 per person; treat this as a broad planning range and confirm menu prices on arrival.
hours: Han Thueng Chiang Mai lists daily service 10:00–16:00 and 17:00–21:30. Hours and menu can change; confirm close to the visit.
bestTime: Lunch or early dinner. December is generally a comfortable season for Chiang Mai outdoor dining, but this is a year-round restaurant dish rather than a seasonal event; the restaurant has indoor seating too.
gettingThere: Han Thueng is at 63/9 Moo 14, Suthep, behind Chiang Mai University near Wat Umong. From Suthep Road, turn into the Wat Umong lane and continue roughly 450 m; a ride-hailing car or taxi is simplest. The venue lists a Google Maps route and has on-site parking per current local listings. No direct public-transit route was verified.
booking: The restaurant lists phone numbers 093-970-6885 and 091-076-6100. No booking requirement was found; call or message ahead to ask whether jin som mok is available that day and its current price.
accessibility: The restaurant is a large sit-down venue with indoor air-conditioned and open-air seating noted in recent listings, and on-site parking. Step-free access, accessible toilets, and other mobility details are not confirmed; contact the venue if these matter.
practicalTips: Ask for จิ้นส้มหมก (jin som mok) or จิ้นส้มหมกไข่ (jin som mok khai); the egg version may be listed separately, and availability can vary.
Fermented pork is tangy and savory; share a small portion with sticky rice and ask staff about chili level.

Choose a freshly cooked, hot parcel. Fermentation is not a guarantee against foodborne illness; avoid raw/undercooked fermented pork, and refrigerate leftovers promptly rather than keeping them warm in Chiang Mai’s climate.
Tell staff clearly about pork, egg, fish sauce, or other dietary restrictions; recipes and cross-contact practices are not documented.
decemberNotes: Plan for ordinary restaurant service in December 2026, not a special event. Verify the split opening hours and ask whether the dish is being prepared that day, since no dated December menu or dish-specific price is published.
uncertainties: The official restaurant website confirms its location and hours but does not establish that jin som mok will be available in December 2026.
Dish-specific price, recipe details, allergens, reservation policy, step-free access, and direct public-transit service were not verified.
The reference image shows jin som mok khai at Anantara Chiang Mai’s Bodhi Terrace, not at Han Thueng; it illustrates the dish only. Reuse permission is not established.
